feedback: Previous visuals looked AI-generated; user asks for complete brief coverage and a more considered design
scope: Three raster proposals, not publication or submission

variants.prompt:
Use case: productivity-visual.
Make ONE SINGLE 16:9 pitch slide as a flat finished raster design. High-resolution landscape, crisp rendered typography. This is the entire canvas, no device, no desk, no perspective.
The previous proposals were rejected as looking AI-generated: robot icons, decorative network diagrams, generic clipart and miniature 3D factories. This revision must feel art-directed by an experienced human editorial/presentation designer.
STRICT VISUAL RULES: typography and layout only. Absolutely NO robots, NO icons, NO diagrams, NO arrows, NO line drawings, NO stock photos, NO rendered warehouses, NO 3D, NO gradients, NO glowing effects, NO glassmorphism, NO rounded-card grid, NO giant finance metric, NO mock browser, NO fake app screenshot, NO QR codes, NO invented logo or brand. Use one refined neo-grotesque family like Inter/Helvetica, bold and regular, excellent alignment and deliberate whitespace. No decorative objects. Only text, thin rules, one restrained color block and one small 3-row decision table.
This pitch is for a company providing operational intelligence to industrial inventory-dependent businesses, starting in French timber and materials. A real small synthetic risk case has been exercised, not a commercial opportunity calculation at industrial scale. Text must not promise verified commercial relationships, savings, customers, deployed ERP connectors or a finished benchmark. A price of an emergency option is not a saving.
All content in English. Use the EXACT concise copy below, with clear hierarchy. Do not add slogans, badges, labels, technical strings or text not listed. Letter badge A, B or C is the sole exception and should be tiny in the upper-right margin.
Exact copy:
Small descriptor: "OPERATIONAL INTELLIGENCE"
Headline: "Turn industry changes into company decisions"
Audience line: "For operations directors in multi-site timber and materials businesses."
Product explanation: "Connect market signals, stock and customer commitments. Protect deliveries and investigate new demand."
Decision example heading: "CONTROLLED DEMO"
Use these EXACT three table rows, each with an action on the left and a result on the right:
"Reallocate reserved stock" / "Conditional: replacement unconfirmed"
"Emergency purchase" / "Feasible: both orders covered"
"Human approval" / "Saved in Aiven PostgreSQL"
Example note: "Real model and tools. Synthetic company and delay. No purchase executed."
Lower section 1:
"DATA"
"Public sources + company records. Typed tools calculate options. Aiven stores evidence and decisions."
Lower section 2:
"WHY NOW"
"Tool-using agents can combine sourced investigation with company calculations."
Lower section 3:
"FIRST USERS"
"Proposed: 3 French timber/materials design partners through founder introductions. Start with one recurring supply decision."
A single small but readable footer:
"Draft. Comparative benchmark and public demo link pending. Opportunity workflow in development."
No em dashes. No footer fragments beyond this one. Keep the slide readable on stage: no tiny or overly light text, sufficient line height, no long body lines. Headline and demo are the two focal points. Audience, data, why now and first-user plan must all be present. The demo is a typeset account of a recorded run, not a screenshot of an invented UI. There is no selected brand name, so don't invent one.
Direction A, badge "A". Pure white, near-black ink and a restrained deep petrol teal accent. Premium investment memo aesthetic. Top-left huge headline with confident asymmetric line breaks and ample whitespace; audience and explanation directly beneath. Upper-right an impeccably typeset restrained decision table with simple horizontal hairline separators, no container border or rounded corners. Give the table a pale grey or pale teal heading row only if necessary, and bold the feasible result. Lower third has three open columns for DATA, WHY NOW, FIRST USERS, with carefully balanced text widths. Use a broad page margin and 12-column grid. Keep a human-designed editorial hierarchy and a single short teal rule. All text must be present and clear.
